question: Why do we ask family planning clients to come back for follow-up visits?

options.B: To conduct major diagnostic surgical procedures
options.C: To permanently discharge the client from care
options.D: To check on the client and offer ongoing support

explanation: Follow-up visits are all about seeing how the client is doing and giving them continuous support with their chosen contraceptive method. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h1)

question: What usually happens if a family planning client never returns for follow-up checks?

options.A: They will experience guaranteed protection from sexually transmitted infections
options.B: They will automatically switch to a permanent surgical method
options.C: They may stop using their method incorrectly or face unmanaged side effects
options.D: They are required by law to pay a large financial penalty

explanation: Without our guidance during follow-ups, clients often struggle with side effects or make mistakes using their contraception, which makes them give up on it. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h1)

question: When is the best time for a first follow-up visit after putting in an IUD (Intrauterine Device)?
explanation: Seeing the client at 4 to 6 weeks lets you check the IUD strings and make sure the device hasn't slipped out. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h2)

question: Why do different birth control methods have different follow-up timetables?

options.A: Because each method carries unique risks, mechanisms, and rates of early side effects
options.B: Because government policy dictates a uniform schedule for all medications
options.C: Because clinics only open on specific days of the week for pills
options.D: Because client preferences change every single week

explanation: Every contraceptive works differently and brings its own early side effects, so our follow-up schedule has to match those critical adjustment windows. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h2)

question: In family planning care, what does 'compliance' mean?

options.A: Whether the clinic follows national healthcare budgeting guidelines
options.B: Whether the partner agrees with the choice of contraceptive
options.C: Whether the manufacturer tests the product for chemical safety
options.D: Whether the client follows the precise instructions for using the method

explanation: Compliance simply means how well and accurately a client sticks to the correct usage guidelines for their birth control. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h3)

question: A client says she still takes her birth control pill every day, but admits she forgets it at least three times a week. How would you describe this?
explanation: She is keeping up with the habit of taking her pills (continuation), but missing doses means she isn't following the schedule properly (poor compliance). [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h3)

question: What is the most common reason clients stop using their birth control method?
explanation: When clients face physical or emotional side effects that they don't know how to handle, they usually stop using the method. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h4)

question: If a client reports mild, normal side effects from her contraceptive, which action is NOT helpful?

options.D: Explaining simple ways to manage the symptoms

explanation: Never brush off a client's feelings! Listening, validating, and supporting them builds trust and helps them stick to their care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h4)

question: Why do nurses need to check for new health changes during follow-up visits?

options.A: Because new health conditions can make a current contraceptive method unsafe
options.B: Because government taxes change based on client medical history
options.C: Because clinic software requires updated home addresses every month
options.D: Because blood pressure readings remain identical throughout a person's life

explanation: New medical issues like high blood pressure can pop up, turning a birth control method that used to be safe into a health risk. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h5)

question: A client on combined oral contraceptive pills reports getting severe migraine headaches with visual changes (auras) lately. What should you do first?

options.A: Schedule her next routine appointment for five years later
options.B: Recognize this as a safety risk and discuss changing her contraceptive method
options.C: Praise her for keeping her follow-up appointment on time
options.D: Recommend she continue the pills without any changes

explanation: Migraines with aura plus estrogen-based pills can sharply increase stroke risk. We need to switch her to a non-estrogen method right away! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h5)

question: When a client wants to switch to a different birth control method during a follow-up visit, what is your main job as a nurse?

options.A: Charge an extra administrative fee for changing the care plan
options.B: Refuse service until a senior medical officer approves the change
options.C: Force the client to continue the original method for at least one more year
options.D: Ensure there is no gap in contraceptive coverage to prevent unintended pregnancy

explanation: When changing methods, timing is everything. We must make sure there is no unprotected gap where an unintended pregnancy could happen. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h6)

question: A client complains that taking a daily pill is too hard with her busy work schedule. What is a great recommendation to discuss?

options.A: Double the daily pill dose to make up for missed days
options.B: Scold the client for being irresponsible with her medication
options.C: Stop using all forms of contraception immediately
options.D: Discuss long-acting reversible options like implants or injectables

explanation: If daily pills are a struggle, methods like injectables or implants take away the stress of daily remembering while offering great protection. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of writing accurate notes during family planning follow-ups?

options.A: Ensuring safe continuity of care when different providers see the client
options.B: Advertising new clinic services to the community
options.C: Providing a colorful drawing book for pediatric visitors
options.D: Reducing the physical weight of clinic filing cabinets

explanation: Clear notes mean that if another nurse or doctor sees the client next time, they can easily pick up right where you left off. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h7)

question: Which of these details is least important to write down in a standard family planning follow-up note?

options.A: Blood pressure and vital health changes
options.C: The brand of pen used by the nurse to write the chart
options.D: Side effects discussed and counseling provided

explanation: We only care about clinical facts! The brand of pen has nothing to do with patient health or safe care continuity. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h7)
